missionPremise: OPS-23 P-152 step 5 of the seven-step ledger-as-serving-path shape (`_decisions/2026-09-11_ledger_as_serving_path_seven_steps.md`): one reader in hauska-engine/services/retrieval-api walks gated cells and dereferences atoms; every surface consumes it. Lane 1 (`_inbox/2026-09-11_p152-reader_close.json`) made cortex a consumer. This lane (P152-PANEL) makes the Property Explorer panel a SECOND, independent consumer of the same reader -- not a consumer-of-a-consumer through cortex -- for the rail families where doing so does not require rebuilding an entitlement gate or duplicating a working, ruled zoning/envelope path this lane has no mandate over.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this close by: (1) GET https://smartsite.cloud/api/spine/property-atoms/<id>/facets for any of the five probe parcels returns X-PE-Read-Path: record and a facets body whose composed fields (cityLimitsFact, floodHazardFact, specialDistrictFact, wellFact, schoolDistrictFact, utilityServiceFact, overlayDistrictsFact, agValuationFact, maxImperviousCoverPctFact, baseFacts.acreage, livingAreaSqft, yearBuilt) match a pre-this-lane production capture on value and source for every field this lane's composer actually sets (see probe.diff below for the full accounting of every difference found, expected or not); (2) an anonymous read of the same endpoint carries `{state:'refused', code:'studio-gated', reason:...}` on all four cadRoll dollar fields, never `null`; (3) `node scripts/surface-probe.mjs --rows P-152 --observations <mcp-observations-file>` (doc_repo) returns a DECIDED (non-UNMEASURED) verdict for all five probe parcels, citing readPath and comparing panel-vs-MCP setbacks.
scopeBasis: This lane converts NINE of the ~14-24 record-slated rails per probe parcel that have both (a) an existing PE wire-type declaration and (b) no entitlement gate: cityLimits, flood, specialDistricts, wells, schoolDistrict, utilityService, overlayDistricts, agValuation, maxImperviousCoverPct, plus baseFacts.acreage and the two structural scalars (livingAreaSqft, yearBuilt, present-only). Explicitly NOT converted, each for a stated reason, not an oversight: (a) zoningDistrict/setbackFrontFt/setbackRules/parcelAreaSqFt/maxHeightFt/maxLotCoveragePct/maxFootprintSqFt -- the zoning-envelope rail group stays atom-chain-owned per R-2 and P-153/P-154's explicit ownership of that surface; (b) marketValue/assessedValue/landValue/improvementValue (cadRoll) and owner -- entitlement-gated in cortex today, and 'the entitlement gate is not yours to change' is an explicit dispatch prohibition; only the null-collapse-on-refusal BUG in the existing cortex-sourced path is fixed, the SOURCE stays cortex; (c) apn/situsAddress/situsCity/situsState/landUse -- P-151/SEAM (already shipped this wave) and P-172/FIND BOX (concurrent this wave) own the address/situs family, and landUse was already flagged 'may remain on cortex temporarily' in this file's own pre-existing module doc before this lane started.

unexpectedDifferencesFoundAndFixed: PR #389: floodHazardFact/specialDistrictFact/wellFact/schoolDistrictFact/utilityServiceFact/overlayDistrictsFact/agValuationFact/maxImperviousCoverPctFact's `source` field read a generic 'parcel_record' string on the first deploy where cortex's existing (already-correct, already-diffed-clean-by-lane-1) value uses a fact-family-specific constant (e.g. 'flood-hazard-fact'). Fixed by vendoring the exact constants from legacy-design-tools' own <rail>FactRead.ts modules.

PR #390: floodHazardFact.floodZone was missing entirely on the first two deploys (flood is a companion rail; the zone lives on the companion row's payload, not the cell_state). Fixed to read the companion row, matching legacy-design-tools' parcelRecordFactRead.ts exactly; a missing/malformed companion row now refuses rather than silently omitting the zone.
disclosedRemainingByteDifferences (not f: floodHazardFact/specialDistrictFact/wellFact lost four classification fields present on the pre-change (cortex) object -- provenanceClass, subjectKind, chainAnchoring, serveLayer. These are added by cortex's OWN pipeline on top of whatever its parcel_record adapter returns (not reproduced anywhere in the vendored reference files this lane read); this lane's /record-sourced path has no equivalent decoration step and none was built. VERIFIED HARMLESS to the declared contract: none of PE's own *FactWire type declarations (atom-chain-to-facets.ts) include any of these four fields, so the client's typed read path was never consuming them either way -- confirmed by reading the type definitions, not assumed.

schoolDistrictFact lost districtCode/geoid; overlayDistrictsFact's absent branch lost cityName. Both are present in the vendored reference adapters (cell.raw.districtCode/geoid; cityNameFromBasis(cell.basis)) but PE's own SchoolDistrictFactWire/OverlayDistrictsFactWire type declarations do not include these fields -- adding them re-triggers the exact excess-property TypeScript error PR #388 fixed. Left out to respect the declared wire contract rather than reintroduce a build defect; a future lane widening those two PE types could restore them.

falsifier: Pre-registered at CP1: if for any probe-set parcel any record-rail's value, source, or vintage on the Property Explorer facets differs from the pre-change capture, or an anonymous read shows a studio-gated cadRoll value as null instead of a typed refusal, or the BFF still calls /atom-chain for a rail the reader served, the port is wrong. Observed: the falsifier FIRED TWICE during this lane's own live verification loop (source-label mismatch on 4/5 parcels, then a missing floodZone value on all 5) -- both found by running the mandated pre/post diff against production, not assumed clean because tests passed and the code read correctly; both fixed and re-verified with the same instrument before being called done. On the final capture, no unexplained value or source difference remains (see probe.diff above; every remaining byte-level difference is either the deliberate fix, a correct label update, unrelated live-timestamp noise already excluded by lane 1's own precedent, or named as a disclosed, contract-respecting omission). The 'still calls /atom-chain for a rail the reader served' clause does not apply literally as written: the atom-chain response never carried any of these nine rails in the first place (confirmed by reading atom-chain-to-facets.ts's own 'what the atom chain alone emits' block, lines ~1996-2036, before writing any code) -- 'retiring' this lane's rails means the cortex-merge copy for them is no longer the SOURCE of the final wire value (proven by the precedence test in pe-property-atoms.test.ts, where a stale pre-existing cortex-sourced cityLimitsFact is overridden by the /record-composed one), not that a whole-parcel atom-chain call is skipped -- that call is still made, once, for zoning/envelope, which this lane does not touch.
contradicted: CI's own Typecheck job never actually type-checks apps/property-explorer/api/** (root tsconfig.json's include is ['src']; api/tsconfig.json is a separate, never-targeted config) -- PR #387's green CI did not catch four real type errors this lane introduced; they surfaced only via `vercel deploy`'s own build-time diagnostic. Fixed the four errors (PR #388); the CI gap itself is named for whoever owns CI config next, not fixed here (out of scope, and the gap is pre-existing -- 3 unrelated errors already live in verdict-layer-merge.ts/pe-share-grant.ts).

The dispatch's item 4 test framing ('a test that fails if the BFF calls /atom-chain for a rail the reader served') assumes the atom-chain response carries the rails this lane converts. It never did -- confirmed by reading the code before writing any -- so the literal test as specified cannot exist; a precedence test (record overrides a stale cortex-sourced value) is the test that actually proves retirement for this lane's rail set, and is what was built.

This lane's own live pre/post diff (not a fixture, not a unit test) found two real defects the unit tests did not catch, because the unit tests asserted the same (initially wrong) values the implementation produced: a generic 'parcel_record' source label instead of cortex's per-family constant, and a missing floodZone value from mis-reading a companion rail as a scalar cell. Both are exactly the DEV_PROCESS class 'a test that cannot fail for the right reason' -- the tests were internally consistent with a wrong implementation.

leave_behind.copiersKeptAliveWithTheirRail: This lane does not touch or retire any of hauska-map's own cortex-merge copiers (floodHazardFactFromCortexRoot, specialDistrictFactFromCortexRoot, wellFactFromCortexRoot, etc. in atom-chain-to-facets.ts) -- they still run, and still supply the field's value for any parcel/rail combination where serve is legacy-transitional or refused, or where this lane's own composer declines to override (e.g. an absent/refused livingAreaSqft or yearBuilt cell). This is BY DESIGN (a rail not slated 'record' must keep serving from its existing path) -- the copiers are not dead code, and a future lane retiring them further needs to first confirm, per parcel, that the slate has grown to cover what they currently serve.

apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/pe-share-view-compose.ts:77 -- a second, independent cortex facets call for the public share-view surface, untouched by this lane and not audited for whether it needs the same treatment.
leave_behind.cadRollEntitlementStillCortexOwned: The four cadRoll dollar rails ARE slated 'record' in the reader for both probe counties today (confirmed live via the retrieval-api /record response), but this lane deliberately did not move their SOURCE off cortex, because doing so correctly requires knowing the caller's Studio/Team/Property-Unlock tier, which the reader has no concept of. A future lane converting these four rails needs to either (a) call cortex's existing entitlement-decision route (the one the panel already calls for other gated surfaces) and apply that boolean to the /record-sourced value, or (b) get an explicit operator ruling that the reader itself should carry entitlement -- 'the entitlement gate is not yours to change' governed this lane's own scope call.
leave_behind.yearBuiltAbsentRefusedNotOverridden: composeLivingAreaSqft/composeYearBuilt only override on a PRESENT, positive numeric cell value; an absent or refused /record cell for these two rails is silently left to whatever the existing structuralFact/verdict-layer path already produced, rather than surfacing the reader's own (possibly different) absence reason. This means a stale or differently-reasoned legacy absence could in principle survive even though the reader now has an opinion -- not observed live on the 5 probe parcels (all 3 Travis parcels' absence reasons matched already: 'CAD row present but structural fields are null'), but not proven absent elsewhere. Deliberate, to avoid inventing a LayerAbsenceWire-shaped absence (verdict/authority/scopeSearched/asOf) this lane has no source data to construct correctly -- named for a future lane, not silently accepted as complete coverage.

rowLevelNote: This lane's OWN mission (panel repoints from cortex-merge to the one reader for its assigned 9-companion + acreage + structural rail set, plus the cadRoll refusal-passthrough fix) is COMPLETE and verified PASS on every probe parcel. status is 'closed-partial' at the OPS-23 P-152 ROW level only because the row's own stated predicate folds in setbacks/zoning agreement (panel vs MCP), which is FAIL on 2 of 5 parcels for a reason entirely outside this lane's scope (F3, pre-existing, assigned to P-154/MOST-CURRENT). Do not read 'closed-partial' as this lane's own work being incomplete -- see completionPredicate and the probe.diff detail above for what this lane specifically closes.
